base_member_text: [L21,L43,L55] (LOW/integer-overflow) An accepted interval count near INT_MAX can overflow the signed loop increment i += numprocs.
audit_member_text: [L55] (MED/integer-overflow) For accepted interval counts near INT_MAX, the final i += numprocs can overflow signed int and prevent reliable loop termination.

adversarial.rationale: The positive interval count is an int accepted by scanf and the final i += numprocs has no overflow protection; INT_MAX with one rank is already a counterexample (icpi.c:21,43-55). Retain as LOW for this interactive demonstration at extreme interval counts, rather than a MED defect in XBeach numerical execution.

base_member_text: [L50-L64] (LOW/input-validation) Negative interval counts enter the calculation branch and print a zero approximation instead of being rejected or treated as quit.
audit_member_text: [L43-L55] (LOW/input-validation) Negative interval counts pass the zero-only exit check and produce a meaningless zero approximation without reporting invalid input.

adversarial.rationale: Only n==0 ends the C loop; for n<0 all positive rank-based starting indices exceed n, sum stays zero and the reduction/printing branch still runs (icpi.c:49-68). The scanf failure fallback handles malformed input, not a successfully parsed negative integer, and the Fortran example's n<=0 guard is in a different executable.
